text:
I


A poem

like a great battle

throws me into this arena

with no enemy but myself,


I

and the great air of words.


II


the cloud lies,

the light lies,

the eyes,

the always deceived,

do not tire of so much fable.


III


stubborn blue,

ignorance of being in another's pupil

like god in nothingness.


IV


I think of wings of fire, of music,

but no,

that is not what I fear,

but the grim judgment of light.

translation.title: Exercises
translation.editorial_note: The translation keeps the numbered exercise structure and the poem-as-battle against the self.
